evidence: Narrowed: the design does state reconciliation's latest-committed-intent behavioral contract (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:15-16; DESIGN-NOTES.md:177-179), so the gap is its missing read boundary, plus /seat's. Reproduction: (1) graph state, templates, overrides, and seat/clone state live in human-readable files in one shared checkout (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:9-10,14,23-25; DESIGN-NOTES.md:28,149-150,202,219). (2) A serialized worker applies a multi-file template/override or name/path mutation and commits it (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:14,23-25; DESIGN-NOTES.md:17-18,58,150); serialization controls writers, but no cited section gives concurrent readers a revision-pinned view or says to wait/retry during that mutation. (3) Separately triggered reconciliation or /seat can read after one file/path changes and before the grouped update commits (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:15,30; DESIGN-NOTES.md:164-165,193,238-239). (4) It can therefore act on a mixture of old and new desired state, or /seat can load an interim path/configuration. Acting on that mixture contradicts the explicit latest committed intent rule (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:16; DESIGN-NOTES.md:179); a /seat load using interim state also fails its latest applicable template/override/rule requirement (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:30; DESIGN-NOTES.md:193,202). This is a possible design-permitted failure, not a claim that the unbuilt implementation already loses data. A coherent committed read or equivalent wait/retry contract remains to specify.
